question: Fuel + 64-slot pool loop gate + VPS fork-cost run: which isolation path is the default for multi-principal P2 handlers, the fresh-Wasm cordon or fork+Wasm?
flips_if: decides fresh-Wasm cordon vs fork+Wasm as multi-principal P2 default

measured.harness: oracles/isolation-fi/rust (isofi, same commit; binaries sha256 in data/binaries.sha256); Wasmtime 49.0.3 (default-features=false: cranelift, pooling-allocator, runtime, std; default 4 GiB reservation + 32 MiB guard; ResourceLimiter 16 MiB); guest = round-004 M0 handler (FNV over 4 KiB, 36 us laptop / 64 us N95); closed loop, 16 concurrent clients, n=3000 per cell; server pinned to 1 core; supervisor-held listening socket; PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0; Landlock + seccomp installed; precompiled module cached locally (fork zygote re-execs after a first compile)

hosts.laptop: i9-14900HX, Linux 6.17.0-14; server on core 2, clients on cores 4-7; 5 interleaved trials per cell; machine shared with other agents' work (1-min load 7-14, recorded per cell)
hosts.kamrui_vps_standin: Intel N95 (4 cores), Linux 6.17.0-41, glibc 2.42; laptop-built binaries; server on core 1, clients on cores 2-3; 3 trials; LAN box used as a VPS stand-in, not a real VPS

measured.budgets: F2 = fuel 15,000,000 units = 2.0 ms of guest work on the laptop (7.44M fuel/ms) and 3.5 ms on the N95 (4.26M fuel/ms), about 58x one healthy request (258,234 fuel). F10 = fuel 75,000,000 (about 10 ms on the laptop). Wall-clock backstop: epoch (cordon) or ITIMER_REAL (fork child), 100 ms

a_loop_gate_laptop.model: throughput ratio ~= c / (c + r*B), where c = per-request cost on the core (cordon 48.8 us, fork 192 us), r = loop rate and B = CPU burned per runaway request. Predicted vs measured: F64-2 0.71 vs 0.72; F64-10 0.33 vs 0.32; FW-F2 0.90 vs 0.90; FW-F10 0.66 vs 0.65. Passing the 0.5x gate at 1% needs B <= 100*c
a_loop_gate_laptop.finding: The research x35 reproduces (x34.2). The fix is a small fuel budget: about 2 ms (~58x the handler) passes. A 10 ms budget fails the throughput gate (x0.32) even with 64 slots. The 64-slot pool alone (epoch-only) cuts p99 from x34 to x5 but leaves throughput at x0.23, which fails

fork_cost_microbench.method: the zygote holds Engine + Module + InstancePre; per request: fork, the child instantiates + runs one healthy call + _exit, the parent waitpid. 3000 iterations per run, medians of 5 (laptop) / 3 (N95) runs, pinned to one core
fork_cost_microbench.laptop_cwasm_zygote: fresh instance in-process 47-53 us p50; fork+exit+wait 57-63 us p50 / 199-200 us p99; fork+Wasm request 149-152 us p50 / 363-403 us p99; overhead vs fresh instance +99-102 us p50, +304-321 us p99
fork_cost_microbench.kamrui_N95_cwasm_zygote: fresh instance 93-106 us p50; fork+exit+wait 142-156 us p50 / 322 us p99; fork+Wasm request 311-316 us p50 / 545-546 us p99; overhead vs fresh instance +205-223 us p50, +301-351 us p99
fork_cost_microbench.module_compiled_inside_zygote: zygote RSS 11.7-11.9 MiB vs 5.7-6.0 MiB with cwasm; fork+Wasm +43-44 us p50 (laptop) / +68-84 us p50 (N95) slower. The zygote must load the precompiled module, not compile it
fork_cost_microbench.pool_vs_ondemand: no material difference (the 258 GiB pooling reservation is a single VMA)

b_fork_wasm.fault_gate_laptop_1pct (5 trials pooled): healthy failures per fault: 0 for panic, abort, segv, loop, oom, poison, hostabort and hostpoison (134-160 faults per class); wrong answers 0; service-gap p99: panic 0.57, abort 0.65, segv 0.60, loop 2.31, oom 3.91, poison 0.77, hostabort 0.63, hostpoison 0.60 ms; loop throughput x0.89; oom throughput x0.79
b_fork_wasm.fault_gate_kamrui_1pct (3 trials pooled): abort, loop, poison, hostabort, hostpoison: 0 healthy failures, 0 wrong; service-gap p99 1.5-1.7 ms, except loop at 6.78 ms (per trial 6.8 / 7.1 / 3.8 ms); loop throughput x0.91; baseline 2,234 rps (cordon 7,478)

c_fresh_wasm_cordon.fault_gate_laptop_1pct (F64-2, 5 trials: healthy failures per fault 0 for panic, abort, segv, loop, oom, poison; wrong 0; service-gap p99: panic 0.09, abort 0.10, segv 0.08, loop 1.13, oom 1.20, poison 0.09 ms; loop throughput x0.71; oom throughput x0.50. An earlier 5-trial run of the same configuration (before the hostpoison class was added; 1-min load 15-19) measured the oom service-gap p99 at 6.6 ms, with a per-trial median of 4.9 ms. Treat cordon oom recovery as marginal
c_fresh_wasm_cordon.host_faults (one cordon process serves m: hostabort: 11.0 healthy failures per fault at 1% (7.0 at 5%), restart service-gap p99 6.2 ms, throughput x0.60. hostpoison: 103.5 wrong answers per fault at 1%; the corrupted host state persists until the cordon restarts. N95: hostabort 11.3 per fault (21 ms gap), hostpoison 101.8 wrong answers per fault
c_fresh_wasm_cordon.fault_gate_kamrui_1pct: abort, loop, poison: 0 failures, 0 wrong, service-gap p99 0.24-1.27 ms; loop throughput x0.84

gate_results_at_1pct.criteria: <=0.05 crash-attributable healthy failures per fault; 0 wrong answers; recovery p99 <=5 ms (service gap: end of the faulting request to the next healthy success); throughput >=0.5x at 1% loop
gate_results_at_1pct.fork_wasm_F2: laptop: PASS on every criterion for the 6 Phase-5 guest classes and both host classes. N95: PASS except loop recovery (6.8 ms pooled p99, over the gate in 2 of 3 trials)
gate_results_at_1pct.fresh_wasm_cordon_F2_64_slots: guest classes: PASS on the laptop (oom recovery marginal across runs: 1.2 ms vs 6.6 ms) and on the N95 for the classes measured there. Host classes: FAIL (11 healthy failures and 100 wrong answers per fault). In a per-principal cordon that damage stays with one principal; in a cordon shared by principals, other principals get failures and wrong answers

decision_effect: ARCHITECTURE section 3.6, row 'P2, multi-principal data'. Replace 'co-equal default candidates ... Decided in Phase 1 by q4-006 ...' with: 'default: fork+Wasm (fork child of an exec-spawned, single-threaded zygote that holds Engine + locally precompiled Module + InstancePre and no compiler state; fresh instance in the child; per-route fuel budget + ITIMER_REAL wall bound; Landlock + seccomp installed in the zygote). Alternative: one fresh-Wasm cordon per principal. A cordon shared by principals is not allowed. Acceptance (oracles/isolation-fi): 0 healthy failures and 0 wrong answers per fault on the 6 guest classes plus hostabort and hostpoison; recovery p99 <=5 ms; loop throughput >=0.5x. Measured cost: +0.10 ms p50 per request (laptop) and +0.21 ms (N95) over a fresh instance; 0.25-0.30x the cordon's throughput for a 36-64 us handler on one core.' Reversal: fork+Wasm overhead >0.3 ms p50 on the q3-001 real 1-vCPU VPS, or the loop recovery gate cannot be met there ⇒ one cordon per principal. The P2 single-tenant row keeps the fresh instance in a per-tenant cordon, with three amendments. (1) Replace 'fuel 10-50 ms' with 'fuel budget per route <= 50x the route's p50 handler cost (default 15M units, about 2 ms for a ~40 us handler); the 100 ms epoch stays the wall-clock DoS bound'. (2) Add 'cordon oom service gap is marginal (1.2-6.6 ms p99 across runs with 16 MiB memories); Phase 5 must hold it under 5 ms'. (3) Add hostpoison to the Phase-5 fault classes. Section 3.6 'Reverse' R3 ('fork overhead <0.3 ms → fork+Wasm default') is met at p50 on both hosts and is borderline at p99 (0.30-0.35 ms).
rung: R1 executed (measurement grade B: laptop + LAN stand-in for a VPS; counts exact, latencies provisional)
reproduce: spikes/q4-006/measure.sh (one heavy.sh job: builds oracles/isolation-fi/rust into spikes/q4-006/target, calibrates, runs the loop, fi and forkcost phases; TRIALS=5 used; deletes target/ and .work/). LAN: LANDIR=<dir> spikes/q4-006/measure.sh copies isofi, guest.wasm, data.bin and run_spike.py to <dir>; on the host: `python3 -I run_spike.py ./isofi guest.wasm $PWD/data.bin data forkcost 3 1` and `python3 -I run_spike.py ./isofi guest.wasm $PWD/data.bin data lan 3 1 2,3`. Summaries: python3 -I spikes/q4-006/analyze.py spikes/q4-006/data (and data-kamrui). Oracle: oracles/isolation-fi/run ; oracles/isolation-fi/run --self-test
limits: Toy handler over a Unix socket on one pinned core. Fork cost grows with zygote RSS (research: 33 ms p50 with a 1 GiB parent; this zygote is 5.8 MiB). The N95 is not a $5 KVM VPS (no steal time, no virtualised page-table cost); q3-001 must repeat forkcost + the lan phase on a real 1-vCPU VPS. The laptop was shared with other agents during the runs. 'Recovery' is defined as the service gap, stricter than restart-only recovery, and it scales with the path's own latency (fork p50 7 ms on the N95). The host faults are simulated through a host function (abort(), or a flag that corrupts later replies); real Wasmtime bugs can be worse (memory disclosure before a crash). Fuel per ms depends on code shape (a tight x+1 loop burned 48M fuel/ms in a first build, against 7.4M for handler work), so budgets need per-route calibration. Wasmtime 49.0.3 was used because 49.0.4 (published 2026-10-19) and 50.0.0 (2026-10-20) are still under the 7-day lock age. 49.0.3 is below the >=49.0.4 security floor (GHSA-897f) and runs only first-party test guests; bump the lock on or after 2026-10-27. The fork child inherits the zygote's Landlock + seccomp; the child-only denylist (socket, bpf, io_uring and others) was not installed. The oracle's reduced run is 1 trial per cell and retries a cell once when it fails only a timing gate (G3/G4).
